target_customer: Specialty chemical and materials buyers in agriculture, cleaning, personal care and polymers
problem: Malonic acid and similar specialty chemicals are made from petrochemicals by costly, hazardous routes such as one using cyanide.
business_model: Manufacturer selling bio-based specialty chemicals and polymer ingredients

founders.name: Eric Steen
education: UC Berkeley and UCSF joint program, PhD Bioengineering
Berkeley Haas Management of Technology program
founders.background_notes: From the YC page; says he built Lygos from a DOE laboratory spinout over about 15 years.

founders.name: Jeffrey Dietrich
education: UC Berkeley, PhD Bioengineering (Jay Keasling's lab)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he is an inventor on 17 patents or applications.

exit.reason: YC page says the company concluded through two strategic sales, one to BioMADE and one to other acquirers; search results show BioMADE took over the Hayward pilot plant and Dober bought the agronomy and water treatment lines. Whole-company status unclear.

technical_complexity.rationale: Engineering yeast to make malonic acid from sugar at commercial yield and scaling fermentation through contract manufacturers is research-grade biotech plus process engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Strain and process patents helped (Dietrich is on 17 patents or applications), but chemical markets are price driven and fermentation know-how is not unique.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying the bio route; Lygos instead sold or transferred assets in 2025 and 2026.

market_need_then: A 2016 AIChE CEP article describes Lygos making malonates from sugar instead of cyanide, producing 1 kg batches for customer validation and planning commercial production through contract manufacturers in late 2016 (summary seen in search).

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and sustainability focused (better materials for better products)

brand_strength.rationale: A B2B chemicals brand known mainly in synthetic biology and chemicals circles; no consumer or community presence found, and the invented name carries no meaning.

pivots.from: Bio-malonic acid as the lead product
pivots.to: Broader performance materials, including agriculture, cleaning and personal care ingredients
pivots.why: Company's own descriptions broadened to performance materials; reason not stated in sources opened.

outcome_analysis: Lygos raised a $13M Series A in 2016 and a $15.5M Series B in 2018, reaching about $40M equity plus government grants by 2018 per the company. It scaled production, added a Ginkgo partnership in 2022 and ended in two strategic sales, with BioMADE taking its pilot plant and Dober buying business lines, after a proposed Flexible Solutions merger was called off. The cause of the wind down is not public, so failure factors stay empty.
notes: Series B press release states total raised $40M equity plus DOE, USDA and NSF funding as of July 2018; YC bio for Dietrich matches ($40M+ equity, $10M federal) while Steen's bio says more than $200M, which conflicts and is unexplained. Aggregators list $33.5M to $230M. Series A date comes from a Hydrocarbon Engineering URL dated 2016-12-16. LG Technology Ventures $5M date not seen.
